title: Frequency Domain ↔ Perspective Shift — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Frequency Domain ↔ Perspective Shift's rich face, its first round at Sketch tier, a proposal: one walk in Teaching Notes, up from a single synthesized kick to a blind test of 'neither view shows everything', with stated procedures run on the same samples beside the reader, and the fingerprint of the words it was laid against. Teaching Notes is one ## with three ###, so its one piece gets one stamp and one approval. The Cartesian and polar point the nomination suggested for The Coordinate System Metaphor was dropped: its numbers hold ((3, 4) is (5, 53.13°)) and a dragged point would show them without testing anything. Frequency-Time Duality's face walks the delay-time axis and is linked, not remade. What the procedures found waits below as offers. I never hold the entry's words.

offers.what: 'Answer: Can't tell from waveform' is true of a glance, not of the waveform. The period is in the samples: a stated procedure (rising zero crossings 150–400 ms after the onset, f = 1 ÷ mean period) reads all 25 test kicks (50–70 Hz, onsets 0–400 ms) to within 0.032 Hz, 25 of 25 nearest right, on the piece's own kick; at 60 Hz one cycle is 16.7 ms. No human has run the piece's blind arm (waveform → fundamental, whole one-second clip unzoomed, 4 of 6 to pass at chance 1 in 5), so whether a reader at that zoom can count the cycles is still open. The lesson line ('Neither view shows everything') stands, read as 'shows plainly'. Proposed: 'Answer: Not at a glance. Zoom into the tail and count: one cycle every 16.7 ms is 60 Hz.'

'Answer: Can't tell from spectrum' holds strictly for what an analyzer draws, the magnitude: across five onsets the whole-clip magnitude spectra agree to 2.7 × 10⁻⁹ dB (rounding), and a template-matching procedure on them scores exactly chance (5 of 25). The two controls that should fail do fail: 60 Hz against 65 Hz differ by 23.1 dB, and with the clip cut at 450 ms, before the kicks end, the onsets part by 51.8 dB and the same procedure reads 25 of 25. The when is in the phase the analyzer leaves out: magnitude and phase together rebuild the kick to 7.6 × 10⁻¹³. Saying so squares this line with The Technical Side's 'no information is lost'. Proposed: 'Answer: Can't tell from the analyzer. It draws each frequency's size; the when is in the phase it leaves out.'

'The same mathematical losslessness holds in both directions: no information is lost' is true of the transform (magnitude and phase rebuild the piece's kick to 7.6 × 10⁻¹³) and not of the frequency view a DAW shows, which keeps the magnitude only: rebuilt from the magnitude alone, all five onsets give one identical pulse at time zero (differences 2.3 × 10⁻¹³). The Structural Identity's row 'Both views contain same information' has the same edge. Proposed, after 'no information is lost': 'in the transform itself, which keeps each frequency's phase as well as its size; the analyzer's picture keeps only the size, and the timing goes with the phase.'

pieces.title: One kick, two views · the demonstration, built and tested
pieces.caption:
**Does each view really fail the other's question?** Six steps on one kick made in the page: a sine falling from 180 Hz to its fundamental, a click, a 500 ms gate. It is drawn as a waveform and as a magnitude spectrum from the same samples. The waveform gives the onset. The spectrum gives the fundamental, and it does not move when the kick does (to 3 × 10⁻⁹ dB, as long as the whole kick is inside the clip). Step 4 rebuilds the kick from its spectrum. With the phase it comes back exactly; from the magnitude alone, every onset gives the same pulse at time zero. Step 5 is the spectrogram, which answers both questions at a price set by its window. The last step is the test: 24 silent trials in four arms, chance 1 in 5, 4 of 6 to pass, stated before the first trial and scored beside stated procedures run on the same samples. The procedures find the spectrum half strict and the waveform half a matter of the glance: counting the cycles in the tail reads the fundamental to 0.04 Hz.

verdicts.why: A fair, leak-free blind test that walks up, but its '0.04 Hz, every time' for counting cycles holds only for its own clean-sine kick (a 2% noise floor drops the same procedure to 5 of 25 while the spectrum stays 25 of 25): scope it to this kick, and stop labelling a ≤2 score on a 'can't' arm 'as the notes say' (a guesser lands there 90.1% of the time).
